The best PS Plus games for kids and families

PS Plus has plenty for younger players, and some of the best are just as much fun for the grown-ups. These are our ten favourites right now, with something for different ages and plenty you can play together on the couch. Each one says the age it's rated for, whether you can play together, and roughly how long it takes. The full list of family games follows.

What counts as family-friendly

This list counts games rated for ages 10 and under: Everyone or Everyone 10+ in Canada and the US. We use Sony's rating for Canada where it has one, and the ESRB rating otherwise.

A rating tells you about content, not difficulty, so some games on the full list are tough for young kids even if they're perfectly suitable. Our picks lean towards games that are easy to pick up and fun to play together.

1

Sackboy: A Big Adventure

Ages 6 and up, co-op for up to 4 · PS4 / PS5 · Metascore 79 · about 11 h main story

Sackboy, the knitted hero of LittleBigPlanet, bounces through bright, crafty worlds to save Craftworld. Up to four people can play together, and the levels set to pop songs are a highlight.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

2

Rayman Legends

Ages 10 and up, couch co-op for up to 4 · PS4 · Metascore 92 · about 10 h main story

A gorgeous, inventive platformer where Rayman and friends run, jump and punch through storybook worlds. The musical levels, where you jump in time to the beat, are pure joy.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

3

Overcooked! All You Can Eat

Ages 6 and up, co-op for up to 4 · PS4 / PS5 · Metascore 84 · about 12 h main story

Up to four chefs try to run a kitchen that keeps falling apart, passing plates and putting out fires. It's chaotic, very funny and a great test of family teamwork.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

4

Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart

Ages 10 and up, single player · PS5 · Metascore 88 · about 11 h main story

Ratchet and a new hero, Rivet, jump between colourful worlds with a huge arsenal of silly weapons. It's like playing a Pixar film.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

5

Untitled Goose Game

Ages 6 and up, couch co-op for 2 · PS4 · Metascore 81 · about 3 h main story

You're a horrible goose loose in an English village, stealing hats, ringing bells and ruining everyone's day. It's short, very funny, and a second player can join as another goose.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

6

Tearaway Unfolded

Ages 6 and up, single player · PS4 · Metascore 81 · about 8.1 h main story

A messenger made of paper travels through a world of papercraft to deliver a message to you, the player. It's charming, gentle and full of creative little touches.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

7

LEGO City Undercover

Ages 10 and up, couch co-op for 2 · PS4 · Metascore 77 · about 15 h main story

Undercover cop Chase McCain hunts a crook across a big LEGO city full of cars, disguises and silly jokes. It's an easy-going open world with a second player able to join on the couch.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

8

Cat Quest III

Ages 10 and up, couch co-op for 2 · PS4 / PS5 · Metascore 80 · about 6 h main story

A purr-ate cat sails a sea full of islands, treasure and puns in a light, colourful action RPG. It's a lovely first RPG, and a second player can join on the couch.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

9

Ape Escape

Ages 6 and up, single player · PS4 / PS5 · Needs Premium · Metascore 90 · about 7.1 h main story

You catch escaped monkeys with a net, using gadgets on the controller's sticks. It's an inventive, funny PS1 classic that still feels fresh.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

10

Bluey: The Videogame

Ages 6 and up, couch co-op for up to 4 · PS4 / PS5 · Metascore 56 · about 1.2 h main story

Bluey, Bingo and their family play games around the house and the neighbourhood in four short episodes. It's made for the youngest fans, and up to four can play together.

Questions

What's the best PS Plus game for young kids?

Sackboy: A Big Adventure is easy to pick up and great with a parent. For preschoolers, Bluey: The Videogame or one of the PAW Patrol games.

What are the best PS Plus games to play as a family?

Overcooked! All You Can Eat, Sackboy and Rayman Legends all let up to four people play together on one console. Our couch co-op list has more.

Are there LEGO games on PS Plus?

Several, including LEGO City Undercover, LEGO Horizon Adventures and LEGO Star Wars II in Premium. They come and go, so check the wall for what's there now.

How do you decide a game is family-friendly?

By its age rating: Everyone or Everyone 10+. That covers content, not difficulty, so some games on the full list are hard for young kids.

Are there kids' games in PS Plus Premium?

Yes, including Ape Escape, LocoRoco, Jak and Daxter and Sly Cooper, from the PS1, PS2 and PSP.
